# v2.99-dev

Housekeeping across a few small areas: who can see what, what leaves the system,
and what happens when an import file is bigger than expected.

## Fixed

- **"Last imported" timestamps are now limited to the companies you can see.**
  This one small read was not company-checked, so it was possible for any
  signed-in person — including a read-only account — to ask whether another
  company had ever had an import, and when. On its own that is a date and a
  yes/no, but company references are sequential, so it also allowed the list of
  companies to be worked out. Asking about a company you have no access to now
  gives exactly the same answer as a company that has never been imported, so
  nothing can be inferred from the difference.

- **Delivery settings now return only the fields the page actually uses.**
  Previously the system returned everything it had stored except a fixed list of
  known-sensitive fields, which meant anything added later would have been
  returned by default. It now works the other way round: a short list of fields
  is shown and everything else is withheld. Passwords and tokens are still never
  sent to the page — it is only told whether one is set.

- **The version number is no longer published to the sign-in page.** It was
  being built into the page itself, so anyone who could reach the login screen
  could read the exact version without signing in — useful mainly to somebody
  matching a system against a list of known issues. It is now sent only to people
  who have signed in. Nothing changes in what you see.

## Changed

- **Spreadsheet imports check the file before opening it.** Import pages now
  refuse a file over 25&nbsp;MB, an empty file, or one that is not a CSV or Excel
  file, and say so. Previously an oversized or mistyped file was read in full
  first, which could leave the page unresponsive with no explanation. This is a
  limit on the browser side only — nothing about what can be imported has
  changed.

## Internal

- The rule that a system-wide administrator also counts as an administrator was
  written out separately in three places. It now has one definition, so the parts
  of the system that enforce it cannot drift apart.

## Upgrading

No action needed.
